propers.name: Introit
propers.text: Gaudeamus omnes in Domino, diem festum celebrantes sub honore beatae Agathae Virginis et Martyris: de cujus passione gaudent Angeli, et collaudant Filium Dei. Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum: dico ego opera mea Regi. ℣. Gloria Patri.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: Let us all rejoice in the Lord, celebrating a feast day in honor of blessed Agatha, Virgin and Martyr. At her passion the angels rejoice and praise the Son of God. My heart overflows with a good word; I speak of my works to the King. ℣. Glory to the Father.

What was NOT checked: the Benziger conformed printing was used only as a boundary check on the extraction, never as a reading; no attempt was made to establish which of several possible loci in the antecedent is the 'original' one, since an order is not a contribution. The 1 content word(s) listed under differences were not recovered from the antecedent layer; the letterforms there are inferred from the surrounding text and from the other witnesses, not read, so this entry is set to medium confidence. This oration is one the Missal draws from a Common; the antecedent witness may print it at the Common, at another saint's day, or at both. That is a difference of position, not of words.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui inter cetera potentiae tuae miracula etiam in sexu fragili
victoriam martyrii contulisti: concede propitius; ut, qui beatae Agathae
Virginis et Martyris tuae natalicia colimus, per ejus ad te exempla
gradiamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.
